$comment: Frozen RB-race benchmark config (Phase 1, docs/benchmark-rb.md). Every run in a model sweep uses EXACTLY these knobs — only the model axis varies, or the table measures the harness, not the LLM. GovSim-style validity: greedy decoding (temperature 0) + N seeded runs + mean/95% CI.

$versionHistory.2: Ollama provider sends think:false to thinking-capable models — reasoning models (qwen3.5 family) previously burned the whole num_ctx window on chain-of-thought and returned empty completions; plain models are byte-identical to v1
$versionHistory.3: World protocol: pristine world restored per block from a pinned-seed snapshot (kills the wear confound), day/weather frozen (kills the time-of-day confound), and memory-service reflections finally run at LLM_TEMPERATURE (compose never passed it — every v1/v2 'greedy' run reflected at 0.7). NOT comparable to v1/v2 for any model: re-bench before mixing rows.
$versionHistory.4: Executor fix: a gather trip that leaves the body where it started now blacklists the whole CLUSTER around its target (radius 8), not just the one block. Per-block marks could not escape a tree — a column of logs hands back the next log every trip — so a bot below an unreachable cliff-top oak burned ten consecutive 60s trips collecting nothing while its team raced a member short (measured 2026-07-26, Ansel). Both gates called those runs clean. This changes how every villager behaves when a target defeats it, so v4 rows are NOT comparable to v3 rows: the model table is re-benched from scratch. The Phase 3b axis results stand as v3 findings in their own report and were not re-run — the tick/ctx conclusions there concern cadence and context window, not gather recovery.
$versionHistory.5: Executor autonomy: when nothing in reach is workable — every candidate blacklisted, or the resource simply not within maxDistance — the body now walks itself toward the nearest workable candidate in a doubled search radius (capped 128 blocks, 20s budget, stopping short so the target lands inside the next trip's ordinary reach) and reports how far it moved. The trip still fails; the next one starts somewhere it can succeed. Fixes the muteness class: measured 2026-07-26, the 'move somewhere new' percept fired 488 times across 15 clean v4 runs and the mind frequently ignored it, leaving villagers deliberating a whole race from a spot that could never serve them (Fen twice with ZERO net travel, Ansel from 97 blocks off-post). Fixed in the body rather than the prompt so no model is advantaged by reading a percept more diligently than another. v5 rows are NOT comparable to v4: re-bench the model table.
$versionHistory.6: Relocation actually works. v5 built the escape hatch and locked it with the key that jammed the door: relocateToward asked the SAME blacklist that had just emptied the picker, so it returned null, never fired once across a whole sweep, and two villagers went mute anyway (v5 r3 Ansel, v5 r3b Fen — the 2-consecutive-mute guard halted the sweep). Now: the blacklist-respecting pick is preferred, but when it comes back empty the body walks toward blacklisted ground rather than standing still — a mark records that a dig failed FROM A PARTICULAR STANDPOINT, not that a block is unreachable in principle, and standing thirty blocks closer changes exactly the thing that failed. On arrival the region marks are cleared (the standpoint that produced them is gone) while per-block marks survive. Validated by replaying the real logged coordinates of both mute runs before any GPU was spent: test/relocationReplay.test.ts reproduces the v5 null-pick, then proves the fallback picks a target. v6 rows are NOT comparable to v5/v4.
$versionHistory.7: Executor: latest intent wins. A gather trip may hold a body for 60s while the mind speaks every 30s, so intents arrive twice as fast as they can run and the per-villager lane grew without bound — measured 2026-07-27, a command aged 617s against the 600s ceiling and landed as STALE_COMMAND while its villager completed nothing all race. A newly arrived command now supersedes one still WAITING for its turn; a RUNNING command is never touched (cancelling mid-dig would strand work and break exactly-one-outcome), and the superseded command still publishes ActionFailed{SUPERSEDED} so the ledger shows the mind changing its mind rather than an intent vanishing. This does NOT raise the trip budget: iron_ore still routinely exceeds 60s for every villager, which remains the accepted ceiling. It removes the cascade that turned that ceiling into muteness. v7 rows are NOT comparable to v6.
$versionHistory.8: Unit 10 — the skill tool-schema layer (docs/architecture/10-skill-tool-schema.md). ONE bump carries every contract change the design pinned, per the batch-executor-fixes rule. (a) DECODE GRAMMAR: bounded small integer ranges become ENUMS instead of minimum/maximum — GatherParams.count 1..8, decision-level importance 0..10, sentiment quantized to quarter steps, and MoveParams.range / FollowParams.range 1..8. That last one was folded into this same bump after the v8 deploy surfaced it live, before any v8 race had been run — and it was not merely unenforced but actively harmful: a pathfinder goal is satisfied the moment the body is ALREADY within range, so an unbounded range turned move into a guaranteed no-op that still reported success. Measured on the v8 deploy 2026-07-31 with the model emitting ranges of 100, 128 and 1000: across a 21-command sample the fleet travelled 6.4 blocks in TOTAL — about 0.3 blocks per move command (18 of 21 exactly zero, the rest under 3.5), at a median command duration of 30ms over a larger 150-command window. Real walks still happen when the model picks a target farther away than its own range (one 10.8-block journey observed), so this taxes movement rather than blocking it outright — but at a third of a block per decision a villager cannot cross the distance to a treeline, and the ledger reports every one of these as 'arrived'. The prompt had never said what range meant (literally '"range": number'), which is how the model learned to invent it; the SYSTEM_TEMPLATE line now states the default and warns that a large range cancels the walk. This is the fix for the measured failure class: of 25,690 decisions in the committed bench windows, 13.0% were malformed and 92.2% of THOSE were numeric-bounds violations, a class no channel enforces at decode time (the Ollama grammar cannot express bounds; the strict frontier wire strips them) while an enum is enforced by both. Expect the malformed rate to fall and the wasted-turn count with it. (b) THREE NEW VERBS — place, store, retrieve — the first dispatched through the ported Voyager skill library rather than a bespoke executor path; chest joins the craft enum because CONTAINER_NOT_FOUND was otherwise advice no villager could act on. (c) FAILURE VOCABULARY: SUPERSEDED finally joins the ActionFailed enum it has been emitting into since v7 (the schema was false about the wire), plus the seven skill-local codes; ABORTED joins the awareness plumbing set in the same commit that lets it reach the wire. v8 rows are NOT comparable to v7: both the decode grammar and the action surface moved.

frozen.$reflectionBudget: Ollama-sized, same reasoning as LLM_DAILY_TOKEN_BUDGET. The shipped default is 200000, which a 15-25 h sweep exhausts partway through — and a tripped reflection breaker is SILENT: memory-service logs 'skipped_budget' and returns no reflections, while AttemptEnded.honestRace only reads agent-service's counters, so the run still passes the honesty gate. Late blocks would then race villagers whose memory stream stopped growing, with nothing in the data to show it.

world.$comment: v3 world protocol. Lowercase, so frozen_env() (bench/sweep_race.py, uppercase-only filter) never exports this object into a container — the sweep reads it as procedure, not as env. Full procedure: docs/runbooks/race-world-reset.md.
world.$resetPolicy: Every model block starts from the same pristine snapshot: stop minecraft, wipe the minecraft-data volume, untar the snapshot, start, wait healthy. Blocked run order stays, but wear can no longer accumulate ACROSS blocks — which is what correlated wear with run index in v1/v2 (bench/results/RACE_REPORT.md, method caveats). Within-block wear survives; interleaving is the upgrade if between-winner ranking claims are wanted.

posts.$comment: Team posts as [x, z] anchors (y omitted = station via spreadplayers, the existing behaviour). PINNED because the world is: letting `locate biome` re-derive posts every run makes the start conditions a function of a command's tie-breaking, and on THIS seed it picks a point that cannot be raced from. Verified 2026-07-26 against the pristine snapshot: both anchors accept `spreadplayers` (1 entity, r=8), both report `locate biome #minecraft:is_forest` distance 0, 872 blocks apart. The auto-located blue post (342,160 / 352,160) is water at y=62 with air above — spreadplayers refuses it with 'too many entities for space, try a spread of at most 0.00', which fails the preflight five retries deep with no mention of water.

world.$timeAndWeather: New in v3. v1/v2 runs drifted through dawn/dusk/night and random rain across a block: light level gates mob spawns, visibility, and (with doDaylightCycle on) how much of a 10-70 minute attempt happens in the dark. Frozen day + clear weather removes it. race-rb2.mjs sets AND reads back both every preflight.

varyingAxis.$comment: The ONE thing a sweep may change per run: the model. Either the global Ollama model, or the per-team split for head-to-head runs.

modelRoster.$comment: Which models a sweep may spend GPU-hours on. Metadata only — lowercase, so frozen_env() (bench/sweep_race.py, uppercase-only filter) never exports it to a container and no configVersion bump is warranted. Every number below was recomputed from bench/results/sweep/manifest.json + the saved slices, not copied from prose; narrative in docs/reports/rb-race-model-sweep-2026-07-25.md.
modelRoster.$approvedEvidence: Wins at configVersion 1: llama3.1:8b 5/5, gemma4:latest 5/5, gemma3:12b 4/5; all 15 runs reached first_coal; winning durations 580.5–1822.1 s.

excluded.evidence: 0/5 wins at configVersion 1 (0/5 runs reached first_coal; 173/176 decisions = 98.3% were schema-violation fallbacks) and 1/5 at configVersion 2 with think:false — best run 4225.4 s vs 580.5–1822.1 s for viable-model wins, 2669/2895 = 92.2% of gather commands failed, 1527/4577 = 33.4% fallbacks.
0/5 wins at configVersion 1, no run ever reached first_coal; 1563/2700 = 57.9% of decisions were schema-violation fallbacks and 1031/1099 = 93.8% of gather commands failed.

sensitivityAxes.$comment: Phase 3b. An axis run overrides exactly ONE knob from `frozen` above; everything else stays at baseline, including the v3 world protocol. Axis runs NEVER enter the model-comparison table (the aggregator partitions on the manifest's `sweepKind`). Metadata only — lowercase, so frozen_env()'s uppercase-only filter can never export this object into a container, and adding an axis does not bump configVersion. Changing a value in `frozen` would.

TICK_INTERVAL_SECONDS.$note: The race harness bounds tick at <=30 by default; the sweep passes --expect-tick <value> so the preflight asserts EQUALITY with the arm instead of relaxing the bound. Slower ticks stretch total runtime, so the per-arm process timeout scales with the arm (see raceTimeoutSeconds in the manifest) — the 75-minute watchdog is inter-milestone, not total, and does not bound a run.

OLLAMA_NUM_CTX.$note: Blocked, not interleaved: changing num_ctx forces an Ollama runner reload, so interleaving would pay a model reload per run. Agent-service deliberation only — memory-service reflections do not read it, so a ctx arm does not widen the reflection window.

THREAT_DEFAULT_STANCE.$status: Design APPROVED, execution DEFERRED by the project owner on 2026-07-26. Run nothing; the sweep keeps refusing this axis. The approved shape is a parallel `variants.mobs` overlay (mobs:true, everything else inherited) selected with --variant, NOT a configVersion bump — a version bump means 'old rows are invalid, re-bench', and mob-free rows are not invalidated by a mobs-on experiment, they answer a different question. Arms brave/cautious(baseline)/guard, 15 runs at N=5, ~5-9h. Full proposal: docs/runbooks/race-sensitivity-sweep.md.
THREAT_DEFAULT_STANCE.$note: NOT RUNNABLE under this frozen config, and the sweep refuses it. Stance governs the hostile-threat response, but `frozen.mobs` is false and the race preflight both disables doMobSpawning and kills every hostile type — so there are no threats for a stance to govern. The only behaviour left is GuardTether's idle-post radius, i.e. a mobility knob under a threat-shaped name. Measuring stance honestly needs mobs ON, which is a DIFFERENT frozen config and cannot share a baseline with the tick/ctx arms. The README's '`guard` costs ~80s on Easy' folklore predates this config and does not transfer.

referenceRecord.$comment: Fastest known honest run under this config (Easy, mob-free).
